newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Mitsui keen to help expand Cape Town port.
newsitem.headline: Mitsui keen to help expand Cape Town port.

text.p: Japanese trading house Mitsui and Co Ltd said on Thursday it was keen to collaborate with South Africa's state-run Portnet harbour company in a plan to expand ship repair facilities in Cape Town.
"It's still at the discussion stage," said Shigeharu Sawai, representative in South Africa of Mitsui's Europe-based division.
"If the project materialises, then there would be a chance for us to supply materials and equipment. We are very keen."
Sawai said the project had initially been proposed by the Japan International Development Organisation Ltd (JAIDO) which had estimated the cost at $8.7 million.
JAIDO, set up in 1989 by the Japanese government and business groups to provide equity support for commercially viable projects in the developing world, has since pulled out of the discussions.
But Sawai said there was still a possibility of obtaining Japanese government aid.

Japanese fishing boats would be among the likely users of the repair yard. A maximum of 90 Japanese vessels are licensed to catch tuna in South African waters as they migrate across the southern oceans.
Johan Carse, acting port manager for Cape Town, said that whatever happened with the Japanese proposals, the city would have to expand its ship repair facilities in the medium term anyway.
It was already sending some vessels which it could not accommodate to the naval dockyard at Simonstown.
"We would be failing in our duty towards the city and the region, not to optimise the port and the facilities it can offer," Carse said.
"We're talking about more than 400 million rand a year that foreign fishing vessels are spending here."
He said ports in Uruguay, Argentina, Mauritius and Reunion were competing with South Africa for fishing boat business and that availability of ship repair facilities was a big drawcard.
"Cape Town has a turnover in excess of 500 million rand a year from ship repair," Carse said.
